exposure: sociodemographic characteristics (age, religion, occupation, education, marital status, dietary habits, family size)
gynaecologic history (menarche, menstrual type, menopause, parity, abortion, mode of delivery)
medical characteristics (chief complaints, clinical examination of cervix, clinical diagnosis, size of uterus)
cohort: The study included 1195 women who attended a Cancer Detection Centre in India between January 1995 and September 2016, with demographics such as 31.4% aged 26-35 years, 91.2% Hindus, and 85.8% married.
finding: Demographic characteristics, addictions, gynaecological/obstetric history, and medical characteristics are strongly associated with increased risk of cervical cancer in Indian women, and Pap smear is an effective screening method for early detection.
mod_finding: Gynaecologic history, including mode of delivery, showed a strong correlation with Pap test findings.
